note: A single site on a large open gravel pad, a former gas well pump station, at the end of a long gravel driveway off Manor Fork Road about 0.3 mile from PA 44, south of Black Forest Village. The agency says it is near PA 44 and adjacent to the Northcentral Regional ATV Trail System: 'Expect road noise and trail noise during ATV season.' Some mapping apps do not route onto Manor Fork Road. Stone fire ring; no table, toilet or water. Pack out trash. --Claude
summary: Site page re-read: MF 001 still listed and bookable online, Drive-In, 'Trailer Site' category only, max vehicle and equipment length 50 ft, pull-in gravel driveway 474 ft, grades Slight, no clearance figure; count 1 and 50 ft confirmed, pull_through false and a sites note added. Year-round confirmed; sells in all five windows. Fees confirmed, $6.50 reservation fee added; hookups and facilities none. Imagery (Esri leaf-on): an open gravel and grass pad about 70 x 35 m in a forest opening, open sky, the pin on it; four vehicles parked along its north-east edge on the image. NHD: nothing within 200 m; not waterfront.
flags: ATV (ruling 1 applied, site KEPT): the page calls the site 'adjacent to the Northcentral Regional ATV Trail System. Expect road noise and trail noise during ATV season.' It does not call the ground a parking area or trailhead, and neither does the DCNR GIS record ('Formerly Gas Well Pump Station. (NumberSites: 10)', GroupCamping Yes). The Haneyville ATV Trail map's only trailhead is on SR 44 at Haneyville, not here. Kept with the agency's ATV wording in the note, as p3-367 kept a site merely beside an ATV trail system. Two things the owner may want to weigh: imagery shows four vehicles parked on the pad, and the 2024 ATV Regional Trail Connector Pilot map linked from the advisories page answered 404, so whether that map marks parking here is UNREAD.
EQUIPMENT (rulings 4 and 8, reported not raised): the page lists 'Looking For Category: Trailer Site' with no 'RV Site' category; Max Vehicle Length 50, Site Access Drive-In. Kept.

Agency access statements (ruling 11: nothing measured, no road surface, gate or bridge research): 'Site Grade: Slight', 'Driveway Grade: Slight', gravel, driveway 474 ft. No caution line. No overhead clearance figure is posted; imagery shows open sky over the pad. The page also carries the district-wide 'Road and Travel Alert' and '4WD vehicles may be recommended for some sites year-round, check notes' boilerplate (this site's notes say nothing about 4WD).
DCNR GIS (2022 edit) lists 'Permit: No' and 'NumberSites: 10' for MF 001; the booking page sells it as one site with up to 8 vehicles and 10 people. The booking page stands.
NAME: the stored name carries the site's own number and road as the booking system gives them ('Site, Loop: MF 001, Manor Fork Road'); nothing to change.

Equestrian/ATV check: the Tiadaghton horseback page names no horse camp; the ATV page names only the Haneyville ATV Trail (trailhead on SR 44 on its brochure map). The 2024 ATV Regional Trail Connector Pilot map linked from the advisories page answered 404 and is UNREAD.

Tiadaghton advisories page (read 2026-11-10): Brown's Run and Sinking Springs Roads closed to snowmobiles with a detour (2024-2025 season); 'Stay alert for ATVs' (ATV pilot uses some PennDOT, township and forest roads); a dust advisory for the Northcentral Regional ATV Trail; Dividing Line Trail closed indefinitely; e-bike rules. No road closure, gate, bridge limit or timber-sale notice on this entry's road. The Tiadaghton camping page publishes no seasonal closure, hunting-season rule or site rotation; it says only 'State forest roads do not receive winter maintenance and are not plowed --motorized, roadside camping access is not guaranteed. Travel at your own risk.'
